nodes.name: CVD Growth of Nb1+xS2 (both 2H and 3R phases)
nodes.procedure: Nb1+xS2 growth was achieved under low pressure in a horizontal furnace (Lindberg/Blue M) with a 25-mm diameter quartz tube. Two small quartz tubes (diameter ~9 mm) loaded with niobium chloride (NbCl5, Alfa Aesar, 99.9%) and sulfur powder (Alfa Aesar, 99.5%) were placed upstream of the furnace. The substrates (SiO2/Si and glassy carbon) were placed face up above an alumina boat in the centre zone of the furnace. The tube was initially pumped to a base pressure of 20 Torr for 30 min. The furnace was heated up to 850°C with a ramp rate of 55°C min^-1 with a flow of 90 sccm Ar. Then, the furnace was heated up to 1,000°C with a ramp rate of 6°C min^-1 under a flow of 90 sccm H2/Ar (10% H2 in Ar). The NbCl5 was sublimated via a heating belt at 260-300°C within 5 min when the furnace reached 1,000°C. After growth for 8 min at 1,000°C, the whole system was naturally cooled down to room temperature. This method produces both 2H Nb1+xS2 (predominantly <20 nm thickness) and 3R Nb1+xS2 (thicker samples).
nodes.source_text: Growth of 2H Nb1+xS2 and 3R Nb1+xS2... We find that the phase of NbS2 is dependent on the thickness of the material... 2H Nb1+xS2 is predominantly observed in crystals with thickness of less than ~20 nm whereas the 3R phase is primarily stable for thicker samples.

nodes.name: CVD Synthesis of 2H NbS2
nodes.procedure: 2H NbS2 was synthesized by CVD using niobium oxide (Nb2O5, 99.9% Sigma-Aldrich) mixed with alkali halide (potassium iodine, KI) and sulfur powder (99.5%, Alfa Aesar). Since niobium oxide has a high melting point, alkali halide is used to create a new eutectic point for the reaction to produce more volatile oxides. The mixture of 150 mg of Nb2O5 and 100 mg of KI powders in the alumina boat was loaded at the centre of the tube furnace and SiO2 substrates were placed above the powder with their polished side facing down. Then 100 mg of S powder was loaded into the upstream region of the tube. To remove oxygen in the furnace, 80 sccm carrier gas 10% of H2 in Ar) was introduced for 20 min. The furnace was heated with a ramp rate of 33°C min-1 to the growth temperatures (1,000°C) and then held at 1,000°C for 30 min before cooling down. The upstream region reached 200°C during growth.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of 2H NbS2. 2H NbS2 was synthesized by CVD using niobium oxide... The upstream region reached 200°C during growth.

nodes.name: Chemical Vapour Transport of 3R NbS2
nodes.procedure: 3R NbS2 crystals were grown by a chemical vapour transport method, which has been employed to prepare other layered compounds. Before crystal growth, a quartz tube containing high-purity source (Nb 99.99% and S 99.99% with a molar ratio of Nb:S of 1:2) was evacuated at 10^-6 Torr and sealed. The sealed quartz tube was then inserted into the tube furnace. The furnace was heated up to 900°C with a ramp rate of 3°C min^-1. The reaction time was 18 h at 900°C and the furnace was cooled down naturally.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of 3R NbS2. 3R NbS2 crystals were grown by a chemical vapour transport method... The furnace was cooled down naturally.

nodes.name: Drop-casting 3R NbS2 on glassy carbon
nodes.procedure: 3R NbS2 was dispersed into toluene and sonicated for 1 h. The solution was deposited onto the glassy carbon electrode (0.1 mg cm^-2) and dried.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cross-sectional HAADF-STEM reveals excess Nb in both 2H Nb_{1.35}S_2 (d_{(0002)}=6.35 Å, c=12.70 Å) and 3R Nb_{1+x}S_2 phases with lower contrast in partially occupied excess Nb planes (occupancy 0.35).
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark field (ADF) cross-sectional scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) images of Nb_{1+x}S_2 clearly reveal excess Nb in both the 2H phase (Fig. 1b) and the 3R phase (Fig. 1c). The spacing d_{(0002)} for the 2H excess Nb phase (6.35 Å, c = 12.70 Å) was found to be close to the theoretical value... The lower contrast in the ADF image of the excess Nb planes is attributed to partial occupation of these sites (an occupancy of 0.35...)

nodes.characterization_summary: Electron diffraction patterns show phase dependence on thickness: 2H Nb_{1+x}S_2 predominant for <20 nm thick crystals, 3R phase for thicker samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electron diffraction patterns corresponding to the phases as a function of thickness are provided in Supplementary Fig. 2d,e. In particular, 2H Nb_{1+x}S_2 is predominantly observed in crystals with thickness of less than ~20 nm whereas the 3R phase is primarily stable for thicker samples.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD spectrum provides evidence for the non-layered hexagonal phase of Nb_{1.35}S_2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction spectrum shown in Supplementary Fig. 3c provides additional evidence for the non-layered hexagonal phase of Nb_{1.35}S_2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Nyquist plots show 2H Nb_{1.35}S_2 has series resistance of 3.5 Ω at 1 MHz and charge transfer resistance of 7.4 Ω cm²; 3R Nb_{1+x}S_2 shows higher resistances.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It can be seen that the series resistance for the 2H phase Nb_{1.35}S_2 obtained at 1 MHz, where the phase angle is close to zero, is 3.5 Ω due to its high electrical conductivity... The charge transfer resistance is 7.4 Ω...
